title: blf: fix coverity resource leak
description:
Make sure value of `channel_name` is only one time created with `ws_strdup()`.

Coverity CID 1648345 (Resource leak)

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • f1822f48 - blf: fix coverity resource leak
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23746/diffs?diff_id=1686433576&start_sha=07d7364d1513fc552036da12e67340bc35198c93)
changed the description

I believe if this happened, it would be a violation of the XML spec because I don't think you can have two attributes with the same name.  The for loop is just walking the (unique) attributes and the channel is properly freed at the end of the outer loop.

`#define ws_strdup(src) wmem_strdup(NULL, src)`

My understanding is that in that for() loop every time we call `ws_strdup((const char*)str_network)` it means `wmem_alloc(NULL, ...)` occurs independently what the actual string (str_network) is. The previously allocated memory is not freed which means resource leak.

That has nothing to do with the actual value of str_network or channel_name, this is a memory allocation issue within a for loop. The channel_name pointer will point to the newly allocated memory address and the previous allocation is left there.

That is why Coverity says too (45.):
```
37. alloc_fn: Storage is returned from allocation function wmem_strdup.[show details]
      	38. var_assign: Assigning: channel_name = storage returned from wmem_strdup(NULL, (char const *)str_network).
      	
CID 1648345: (#1 of 1): Resource leak (RESOURCE_LEAK)
45. overwrite_var: Overwriting channel_name in channel_name = wmem_strdup(NULL, (char const *)str_network) leaks the storage that channel_name points to
```

Currently, the `g_free(channel_name)` is in the outer for loop and not in the inner for loop
where it's actually used.

So to me the right way is to free up channel_name every time before wmem_strdup().

I think the MR make sense and would also fix the coverity resource leak warning.

(Sorry, my gitlab notifications have mysteriously gone away)

My point is that we only call
`ws_strdup((const char\*)str_network)`
when the "network" XML attribute is present in the XML and XML attributes can't have duplicate names.
So the
`for (xmlAttrPtr attr = current_channel_node->properties; attr; attr = attr->next)`
loop can only possibly allocate 1 channel unless it's violating the XML spec (in which case the parsing won't succeed and we'll never hit this for loop in the first place)

If you or the WS developers disagree with my code change to address a Coverity warning, I will accept it. Just tell me to close the MR in that case.

There is nothing more I can do with good faith.

@mmann78 can you please elaborate further why you think the "code analysis is incorrect/incomplete"?

Within that inner for loop `ws_strdup()` could be called multiple times if we have more than one "network" attribute. Each time it is called, allocator is NULL which means it is not going to be freed up automatically. To me this is quite clear and since at this point of the code we cannot know if there was an earlier loop with `ws_strdup()` called, we have to handle that case by adding there a `g_free(channel_name)`.

Line 3240 (outer for loop) has `g_free(channel_name)` which frees up the memory which was allocated with `ws_strdup()` the last time. But that does not free up any earlier allocations for sure.

Please tell me where my logic is wrong and why do you think `g_free(channel_name)` is not required?

May I seek addition comment from @AndersBroman , @johnthacker , @JaapKeuter , @martin.r.mathieson, @oakimk , please? Thank you.
I'm completely out of time for doing Wireshark reviews for now.

Your logic isn't sound because attributes are required to be unique by the XML specification.  This is not a "generic" for loop where the "network" attribute can be repeated. Coverity is wrong because of that fact.  I don't know how to tell Coverity it's wrong in a way that will remove the CID so this issue isn't revisited again.

I thought since the issue is with XML, that the capture file format would be text based (and I could manually modify it to prove my point).  I have a capture file locally that I must have gotten from gitlab MRs/issues, but I can't seem to find it (Wireshark_BLF_apptext_segmentation.blf).  However, it is a binary (compressed?) format so I can't add a second "network" tag to show that XML parsing will fail and the for loop will never be hit.
If you are able to share that .blf file, then I can have a look if I could alter it for this test.
found it: [work_item:19379]

```
eXtensible Markup Language
    <?xml
        version="1.0"
        encoding="UTF-8"
        ?>
    <channels
        version="1">
        <channel
            number="1"
            type="CAN"
            network="CAN">
            <databases>
            </channel>
        <channel
            number="2"
            type="CAN"
            network="Network2">
            <databases>
            </channel>
        <channel
            number="3"
            type="CAN"
            network="Network3">
            <databases>
            </channel>
        </channels>
```

The MR is for `wiretap\blf.c` so I am not sure a .blf file dissection can help us to validate here anything.... this is not `epan\dissectors\file-blf.c`

I was able modify that .blf file and the modified file is decoded like this:
```
<channel
    number="2"
    type="CAN"
    network="Network2a"
    network="Network2b">
    <databases>
    </channel>
```

There are 2 "network" attributes in it...

while the original file shows:
```
<channel
    number="2"
    type="CAN"
    network="Network2">
    <databases>
    </channel>
```
Any comment, please?
